transport-modes.alt: Four panels. Passive transport: particles crowded outside move into the cell, where they are sparse, with no ATP. Active transport: particles sparse outside are moved into the cell, where they are crowded, by a transport protein using ATP. Endocytosis: the membrane folds in around a particle and pinches off a vesicle. Exocytosis: a vesicle fuses with the membrane and releases its contents outside.
